title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies
abstract: arXiv:2611.07540v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study action-conditioned monitoring of autonomous-vehicle behavior in semantically unusual driving scenes. The target is whether the executed ego action is appropriate for the scene: the same scene can admit both normal and anomalous behavior, so visual unusualness alone does not determine the monitoring label. A Vision-Language Model (VLM) first predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video window; the monitor then compares that expectation with the realized ego-motion trajectory under an explicit compatibility rule. To study this monitoring task, we contribute a six-field taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios spanning both failure polarities (42 derived from documented incidents), a generated video corpus with estimated trajectories, and an exploratory two-stage monitor on that corpus. On 235 clips from 15 scenario families, the two-stage protocol with a fixed T-2.5 s window obtains 83.0% accuracy and anomaly recall 0

translated_title: 面向自动驾驶车辆语义异常的动作条件视觉语言模型监测
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在语义异常的驾驶场景中对自动驾驶车辆行为进行动作条件监测的问题。监测目标是判断自车执行的动作是否适合当前场景：同一场景可能同时容许正常与异常行为，因此仅凭视觉上的异常性并不能决定监测标签。视觉语言模型（VLM）首先从一个隐藏了结果（结局）的视频窗口中预测场景所需的动作；随后监测器在明确的兼容性规则下，将该预期与实际的自车运动轨迹进行比较。为研究这一监测任务，我们贡献了：（1）一个涵盖两种失败极性的112个配对场景的六字段分类法（其中42个源自有记录的真实事故）；（2）一个带有估计轨迹的生成视频语料库；（3）在该语料库上的一个探索性两阶段监测器。在来自15个场景族的235个视频片段上，采用固定T−2.5秒窗口的两阶段协议获得了83.0%的准确率和异常召回率0
tldr: 该论文提出一种动作条件监测框架：先由视觉语言模型从隐藏结果的视频片段中预测场景所需动作，再通过明确的兼容性规则将预期与实际自车轨迹对比，从而判断自动驾驶行为在语义异常场景中是否恰当，并配套构建了112个配对场景的分类法和生成视频语料库。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an action-conditioned monitoring framework in which a VLM predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video window, and an explicit compatibility rule compares this expectation with the realized ego-motion trajectory to judge whether autonomous driving behavior is appropriate in semantically unusual scenes, supported by a taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios and a generated video corpus.
